newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices fall with warm weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices fall with warm weather.

text.p: Most Canadian spot natural gas prices retreated Wednesday from last week's highs as temperatures rose in western Canada and the U.S. long weekend approached, marketers said.

Gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted at C$1.92/1.97 per gigajoule, down sharply from C$2.67/2.72 per GJ last week. December AECO was also talked down at C$1.94/1.98, a big drop from C$2.65 per GJ on November 20.
"With weather like this there's a lot more downward pressure than upward pressure," said a Calgary-based trader. "I think it's going to get pretty cheap by the weekend."
Temperatures in Alberta rose to above freezing on Wednesday and Environment Canada forecast continuing mild weather through Sunday.

Big drops in price were also reported in British Columbia. Gas for export at the Huntington/Sumas border point was discussed in the US$2.30/2.45 per million British thermal unit range, a sharp drop from highs of US$4 last week. December Sumas fetched anywhere from US$2.50 to US$3.

The exceptions to lower prices were U.S. Midwest and Northeast gateways such as Emerson, Manitoba and Niagara, Ontario, which were about 45 cents higher on average than last week. --Calgary Bureau 403-531-1624
